name: EU DORA — Digital Operational Resilience Act
description: Standalone DORA overlay for EU financial entities subject to the Digital Operational Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554). Enforcement date: January 17, 2025. Applies to banks, investment firms, insurance undertakings, payment institutions, electronic money institutions, crypto-asset service providers, and critical ICT third-party service providers. This overlay provides DORA-specific evidence requirements beyond the combined GLBA/SOX/DORA bundle — use when the regulated entity is an EU financial entity and DORA-specific auditor evidence is required. Key additions: ICT incident notification timeline requirements (Art. 19), DORA testing program (Arts. 24-26), and ICT third-party risk management (Arts. 28-30).

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: ICT-related incident classification and reporting per DORA Art. 18-19. Major incidents require: initial notification within 4 hours of classification, intermediate report within 72 hours, and final report within 1 month. Competent authorities are the relevant national supervisory authority (e.g., national central bank, financial regulator). EBA/ESMA/EIOPA exercise supervisory convergence.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Competent authority designated under DORA Art. 46 in the member state where the financial entity is established. EBA single point of entry for cross-sector incidents under Art. 19(6).

human_oversight_mandates.description: DORA Art. 5(2) assigns direct responsibility for ICT risk management to the management body. Art. 17(3) requires the ICT-related incident management process to include management escalation and oversight. Art. 15 requires anomaly and deviation management with management body review of outcomes. Management body members must maintain sufficient knowledge of ICT risk (Art. 5(4)).

notes: DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554) is a directly applicable EU regulation — no transposition required. Enforcement began January 17, 2025. The management body of the financial entity has direct personal accountability under Art. 5(2). Key DORA-specific items not covered in the GLBA bundle: (1) ICT incident notification timeline — 4h initial alert, 72h intermediate, 1 month final to competent authority; (2) DORA digital operational resilience testing program including TLPT for significant entities; (3) ICT third-party service provider register and Art. 30 mandatory contract provisions; (4) Concentration risk management for critical ICT third-party service providers; (5) 5-year record retention for critical function records (Art. 12(6)). This overlay is DORA-standalone. The glba.json combined overlay remains appropriate for entities facing combined GLBA/SOX/DORA evidence requirements.
